milestone.title: Skill catalog + deployment manifest: mp install tracks what it deploys, adds opt-in catalog skills

intent.outcome: mp install writes and reads a deployment manifest (~/.agents/master-plan/installed-skills.json) recording every deployed skill with provenance, category, source, and version. Skill manifests grow a 'category' field (core | catalog). Bare 'mp install' deploys core skills only; catalog skills are opt-in via --skills. Two vendored catalog skills ship verbatim under MIT attribution: diagnosing-bugs and codebase-design (from mattpocock/skills). mp install --list-skills lists the registry annotated with per-harness deployment state. mp install --check gains deployment-drift detection (missing / stale / orphaned). mp uninstall prunes against the manifest instead of re-deriving from the embedded registry. Open questions: (1) should the manifest track a content hash per deployed SKILL.md, or is id+version enough for drift detection? (2) for bare mp install deploying only core skills, is this a breaking change worth a migration note, or do we add a --all flag preserving old behavior?

problem.description: Two gaps. (1) Provenance drift: mp install is fire-and-forget — it copies SKILL.md into harness dirs but records nothing, so there is no way to answer 'what is deployed?' or reconcile after a consolidation milestone. M141 dropped master-planner + mp-handoff + mp-code-review from the source registry, but installed MP_HOME copies linger because nothing pruned them — live drift on the maintainer's own machine. Catalog skills with upstream versions make this worse, not better. (2) No opt-in tier: good adjacent skills (diagnosing-bugs, codebase-design — MIT, dependency-free, no plan-zone collision, no core-skill overlap) have no home. mp only deploys its own workflow backbone today.

in_scope: Deployment manifest: ~/.agents/master-plan/installed-skills.json. Schema: array of { skill_id, harness, category, source, source_url, upstream_version, installed_at }. Written by install (read-modify-write), read by list/check/uninstall, pruned by uninstall.

Skill manifest.json grows a 'category' field: 'core' (default-deployed) | 'catalog' (opt-in). Default to 'core' when absent for backward compatibility. Add 'source', 'source_url', 'upstream_version' fields for catalog skills.
Behavior change: bare 'mp install' deploys ONLY core skills. Catalog is opt-in via --skills <id,...>. Document in CHANGELOG.

Vendor two catalog skills verbatim (no content adaptation — mp serves any language): templates/skills/diagnosing-bugs/ (SKILL.md + scripts/hitl-loop.template.sh) and templates/skills/codebase-design/ (SKILL.md + DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md + DEEPENING.md). Source: mattpocock/skills (MIT).
Attribution: THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md at repo root carrying the MIT notice for mattpocock/skills; header comment in each vendored SKILL.md pointing back to upstream.
mp install --list-skills: prints id / display / category / deployed-to (per harness) / source. Reads manifest for deployment state.

mp install --check extended: existing source-registry validation PLUS a deployment-drift phase reporting (a) deployed-but-removed-from-registry orphans, (b) registry skills not yet deployed, (c) hash mismatch if tracked.
mp uninstall: reads installed-skills.json, removes exactly what was deployed, prunes manifest entries. Survives registry changes across versions (fixes the M141 stale-copy problem).
mp install --skills validates against core + catalog; unknown id errors list available catalog skills.
out_of_scope: No new top-level command (mp skill ...). Everything extends mp install. A dedicated verb family is a LATER milestone, earned only when list/remove/update becomes painful.
No network fetch. Catalog skills vendor into templates/skills/ and ship in the tarball. No git clone, no version pin against a remote. Offline-first.
No marketplace / mp skill search. That is skills.sh's lane. mp ships a curated catalog, not a registry.
No content adaptation of vendored skills — ship verbatim. The two catalog skills are language-agnostic.
No project-scoped skills in plan.toml. Skills are environment config (~/.agents/), never plan data.
No additional catalog skills beyond diagnosing-bugs and codebase-design.

design_decisions.choice: Vendor catalog skills verbatim, do not adapt content
design_decisions.rationale: mp serves projects in any language; the two seed skills are language-agnostic (diagnosing-bugs has zero ecosystem refs; codebase-design has 3 illustrative TS refs that are not load-bearing). Adapting to Rust would make the skills worse for non-Rust mp users and create a fork to maintain. Vendoring verbatim means re-vendoring is a clean file copy + version bump.
mp ships vetted skills like a Linux distro's package set. mattpocock's skills.sh already does marketplace well. Catalog seeds at 2 skills and grows only when a real need surfaces, never to pad.

design_decisions.choice: Extend mp install, do not add a new mp skill verb family yet
design_decisions.rationale: Keeps surface area minimal. A dedicated mp skill list/add/remove earns its existence only when managing installed skills becomes painful — a later milestone, not this one.

design_decisions.choice: installed-skills.json is environment config under ~/.agents/master-plan/, never plan data
design_decisions.rationale: Respects the two-zone rule. Skills are agent-environment config shared across projects, not per-project plan state.

design_decisions.choice: bare mp install deploys core skills only; catalog is opt-in via --skills (breaking change, documented in CHANGELOG)
design_decisions.rationale: The maintainer's own machine has stale M141 copies because install was fire-and-forget. Defaulting to core + opt-in catalog stops catalog skills accumulating unmanaged; the --all flag is NOT added to preserve a clear 'core = always, catalog = choose' contract.

design_decisions.choice: catalog skills vendor into templates/skills/ and ship in the tarball; no network fetch, no git clone, no remote version pin
design_decisions.rationale: mp stays offline-first. marketplace/search is skills.sh's lane; mp ships a curated catalog with provenance, not a registry with live resolution.

design_decisions.choice: open question: manifest tracks id+version only by default; content hash is a candidate enhancement, not v1
design_decisions.rationale: id+version answers 'what is deployed' and reconciles the M141 stale-copy case. A content hash adds stale-detection precision but is extra surface; defer until drift detection proves insufficient.

steps.action: Define installed-skills.json schema (skill_id, harness, category, source, source_url, upstream_version, installed_at) and wire an atomic read-modify-write into the install path so every deployed skill is recorded with provenance.
steps.done_when: mp install writes installed-skills.json; a fresh install then read-back returns every deployed skill with all provenance fields

steps.action: Add category (core|catalog), source, source_url, upstream_version to skill manifest.json (default category=core for back-compat). Make bare 'mp install' deploy only core; catalog via --skills <id,...> with validation against core+catalog.
steps.done_when: bare mp install skips catalog skills; --skills diagnosing-bugs deploys it; unknown id errors listing available catalog skills

steps.action: Vendor templates/skills/diagnosing-bugs/ (SKILL.md + scripts/hitl-loop.template.sh) and templates/skills/codebase-design/ (SKILL.md + DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md + DEEPENING.md) verbatim from mattpocock/skills (MIT). Add THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md at repo root + header attribution comment in each SKILL.md. manifest.json category=catalog for both.
steps.done_when: both skills present verbatim; attribution file + headers exist; manifests carry category=catalog

steps.action: Implement mp install --list-skills: print id, display, category, deployed-to (per harness from the manifest), source. JSON by default.
steps.done_when: mp install --list-skills lists core + catalog skills with deployment state per harness

steps.action: Extend mp install --check with a deployment-drift phase: (a) deployed-but-removed-from-registry orphans, (b) registry skills not yet deployed, (c) stale/hash mismatch if tracked. Keep the existing source-registry validation passing with the two new catalog skills and their consumes/Pattern refs.
steps.done_when: mp install --check reports orphans/un-deployed/stale against the manifest; source-registry validation passes with catalog skills

steps.action: Rewrite mp uninstall to read installed-skills.json and remove exactly what was deployed, then prune the manifest entries. Must survive registry changes across versions (fixes the M141 stale-copy problem where dropped source skills linger).
steps.done_when: mp uninstall removes only manifest-listed skills; a registry skill dropped post-install is still pruned via the manifest

findings.description: F-04: InstalledSkillsManifest::load() in install.rs:87-93 silently resets a corrupt manifest to empty via unwrap_or_default(). The doc says 'first install on a fresh MP_HOME' but the code also swallows JSON parse errors from a present-but-corrupt file — silent data loss of all deployment provenance. Fix: distinguish file-missing (Ok(default)) from file-present-but-unparseable (Err).
findings.author: external-review

findings.description: F-06 (backlog observation, NOT a fix for this review): check_registry drift phase (install.rs:321-333) warns 'registry skill X is not deployed anywhere' for every catalog skill on any fresh --check, since catalog skills are opt-in by design. This creates warning fatigue (the test at install_manifest.rs:287 even locks the behavior in). Per AC-04 this is spec-compliant, so not blocking — but a future milestone should split core-undeployed (drift) from catalog-available (info) so a healthy fresh install isn't noisy.
findings.author: external-review

findings.description: F-05: check_registry in install.rs:312 and :334 declares two distinct HashSet variables both named `known_ids` (first HashSet<String>, then HashSet<&str>), the second shadows the first. Rename the first to avoid the shadow.
findings.author: external-review

findings.description: F-03: InstalledSkillsManifest::record() and forget() each call save() (full serialize + atomic_write) on every invocation. In install.rs:559 record() is called inside a nested loop (harnesses × skills), so a default install does N×M atomic manifest writes; --harness all with 5+ skills = 40+ writes of growing JSON. Forget() in uninstall has the same pattern (install.rs:629, 658). Fix: mutate entries in-memory inside the loop, save once after the loop completes.
findings.author: external-review
